blocks.title: Independent Repositioning With Global Reach
blocks.body: Independents repositioning into Hotel Indigo gain IHG reach when the asset already has character and the PIP can make that character brand-legible. Diligence conversion capital, design narrative, and labor before underwriting peer demand comps. Owner value fits when affiliation sharpens commercial tools without erasing local identity. Weaker when underwriting assumes soft-brand flexibility while Indigo standards still drive material scope.

blocks.title: Mixed-Demand City Hotel
blocks.body: Mixed-demand city hotels fit Indigo when leisure storytelling and weekday corporate demand can share one design-led box. Confirm conversion PIP, capital reserves, and operator depth for lifestyle service and IHG systems after cutover. Weaker when markets cannot support the design and public-space investment Hotel Indigo presentation requires after affiliation.

blocks.title: Typical Use Case
blocks.body: A city, gateway, or culturally distinctive hotel where the owner wants to strengthen guest relevance through a locally grounded story while considering the support of an IHG brand platform.

blocks.title: Why Value Is Strongest in These Scenarios
blocks.body:
Keep Local Product Intent—Add IHG One Rewards: retain Hotel Indigo's brand promise while accessing loyalty earn/redeem and parent commercial systems a standalone hotel cannot buy alone.
Neighborhood boutique: local design cues, neighborhood storytelling, and upscale-lifestyle stays with IHG One Rewards distribution.
Sibling Clarity: diligence fit versus same-parent peers before assuming identical owner use case or fee path.
Operator & Owner Fit: strongest when the asset can deliver the brand's guest promise with QA discipline—weakest when sponsors want the flag without the product investment.
Disclosure Discipline: model economics only from current fee exhibits—Factory 2.0 does not invent undisclosed percentages.

For conversions, sequence Hotel Indigo design narrative, PIP, FF&E, signage, and IHG systems cutover with financing and brand approval gates. Keep the asset’s neighborhood story visible—do not default to a generic IHG shell.

Hotel Indigo is an IHG lifestyle brand focused on neighborhood storytelling and local discovery—not InterContinental or a generic IHG prototype. Use this checklist to diligence brand fit, design expectations, and operating implications. Confirm every row with current Hotel Indigo / IHG development materials and your agreement before capital commitments.

blocks.title: Owner Considerations
blocks.body:
Validate the neighborhood narrative against the real location, design, and F&B plan.
Confirm opening versus phased standards and systems cutover timing.
Underwrite operator capability for lifestyle service, not only rooms operations.

Which Hotel Indigo design / neighborhood standards apply to this address?
What is mandatory at opening vs phased over 12–24 months?
How do F&B or local-experience expectations change PIP scope?
What IHG One Rewards and technology cutover dates are contractual?
What opening readiness and quality-review expectations should owners plan for?

blocks.title: Neighborhood / Design Storytelling
blocks.body:
Typical consideration: Each Hotel Indigo is expected to express a clear neighborhood narrative through design, art, and guest experience—not a shared IHG shell look.
Owner planning consideration: Confirm the local story, design direction, PIP scope, and whether conversion retains authentic neighborhood character.
Typical status: Confirm With Brand
Notes to confirm: Avoid InterContinental or other IHG brand imagery/standards confusion.

blocks.title: Guestroom / Suite Standards
blocks.body:
Typical consideration: Guestroom finishes, bath, bedding, and FF&E follow Hotel Indigo lifestyle standards within the IHG system.
Owner planning consideration: Confirm renovation scope, procurement path, room mix, and conversion flexibility for this asset.
Typical status: Confirm With Brand
Notes to confirm: Project-specific design review is common on conversions.

blocks.title: Lobby / Public Space
blocks.body:
Typical consideration: Arrival and public spaces should support local discovery, social use, and brand storytelling.
Owner planning consideration: Confirm lobby layout, seating, work zones, FF&E, and design-review gates for conversion or new build.
Typical status: Typically Expected
Notes to confirm: Subject to Hotel Indigo design review—not a corporate InterContinental lobby brief.

blocks.title: F&B / Local Discovery
blocks.body:
Typical consideration: F&B or local-experience programming often reinforces neighborhood positioning.
Owner planning consideration: Confirm outlet concept, kitchen/support space, staffing model, and whether offerings are required at opening.
Typical status: May Apply
Notes to confirm: Scope varies by market and conversion path—confirm with IHG Hotel Indigo development.

blocks.title: Technology / IHG One Rewards
blocks.body:
Typical consideration: IHG systems and IHG One Rewards participation typically apply across Hotel Indigo.
Owner planning consideration: Confirm PMS/CRS cutover, loyalty integration, Wi-Fi/reporting, training, and timing relative to opening.
Typical status: Typically Expected
Notes to confirm: Systems obligations sit with IHG—not a separate InterContinental stack.

blocks.title: Training / QA / Opening Readiness
blocks.body:
Typical consideration: Opening readiness, brand training, and quality reviews typically apply before and after opening.
Owner planning consideration: Confirm opening checklist, training cadence, inspection process, and remediation expectations.
Typical status: Typically Expected
Notes to confirm: Timing can affect opening plan and working capital.

blocks.title: Evaluation
blocks.body: Start diligence with district authenticity, building suitability, and whether the asset can deliver a credible neighborhood-led full-service stay under Hotel Indigo and IHG public positioning. Confirm development interest, franchise or management path, and how local storytelling will appear in public spaces, F&B, and guest communications before committing design capital or relying on IHG One Rewards participation.

blocks.title: Conversion Design
blocks.body: Shape conversion and design around Indigo's place-led guest journey—facade, lobby, corridors, and activation spaces should read as locally rooted while meeting IHG lifestyle design review. Align PIP scope, operator capacity, and financing with the intended F&B and programming mix rather than treating the flag as cosmetic repositioning alone.

blocks.title: Pre-Opening
blocks.body: Sequence IHG systems cutover, brand training, hiring, and soft-opening plans with design sign-off and operating readiness. Budget time for loyalty integration, commercial setup, and QA touchpoints. Third-party operators often lead daily pre-opening execution while the owner funds capital and confirms milestone approvals with IHG development.

blocks.title: Opening
blocks.body: Execute opening with consistent neighborhood storytelling across service, F&B, and public-space programming while stabilizing IHG systems and guest-facing standards. Opening support typically blends brand QA, training reinforcement, and commercial launch coordination—confirm who leads each workstream in the specific agreement.

blocks.title: Ramp-Up
blocks.body: During ramp-up, calibrate rate positioning, channel mix, and local programming against stabilized service delivery and IHG revenue-management participation. Owners should watch labor, F&B complexity, and guest-review themes tied to the district narrative—not only occupancy headlines.

blocks.title: Ongoing
blocks.body: On an ongoing basis, refresh local programming and physical product within brand guardrails while meeting IHG reporting, QA, and loyalty obligations. Revisit PIP timing, operator fit, and district competitiveness when markets shift or ownership strategy changes.

blocks.title: What Owners Are Buying
blocks.body: Hotel Indigo gives owners a lifestyle soft-brand path that connects a neighborhood story to IHG distribution and loyalty. The owner proposition is local character with platform reach—subject to brand standards, systems, and conversion requirements confirmed for the specific asset.

blocks.title: Owner outcomes
blocks.body: Owners buy Hotel Indigo for neighborhood lifestyle positioning plus IHG distribution and One Rewards member access—outcomes still depend on local demand, conversion/PIP scope, and operator execution of the neighborhood story.

blocks.title: Neighborhood Urban Conversion
blocks.body: Hotel Indigo creates owner value on urban conversions where neighborhood narrative and design-led lifestyle product can lift rate positioning—IHG distribution fits when lobby, F&B, and guestroom standards can be delivered without overbuilding full-service banquet scope.

blocks.title: Gateway Lifestyle Development
blocks.body: Gateway and cultural-corridor sites suit Indigo when new-build or adaptive projects need IHG lifestyle positioning rooted in place—owners underwrite capital and labor carefully so affiliation lift matches realistic rate support after cutover.

blocks.title: Lifestyle Portfolio Standardization
blocks.body: Multi-asset sponsors use Hotel Indigo to standardize neighborhood lifestyle stays across cities—value holds when operator depth, conversion capital, and IHG systems cutover are priced honestly rather than assumed as a light reflag.

blocks.title: Third-Party Operator-Led
blocks.body: Indigo suits assets run by operators who can balance IHG brand standards with local neighborhood storytelling—sponsors need affiliation lift and financing credibility while keeping design character and service intensity inside underwriting.

Neighborhood storytelling must be backed by real product and service delivery—not only marketing language
Confirm prototype, public-space, and F&B expectations for the conversion scope
Do not assume soft-brand flexibility removes systems, loyalty, or quality-review obligations
Compare Indigo with sibling IHG lifestyle options on capital intensity and operator fit
